ja: האהל, וקאל אלחכים ען ג'מלהֵ אלעואם ועבד אויל לחכם לב. והד'א אלקסם מן אקסאם אלתואצ'ע ואן כאן ואג'בא פי אלטבע, פליס מן אלפצ'איל אלעאליה עלי אלאטלאק, לאנה גיר שאמל לג'מיע אלנאטקין ולא ואג'ב עליהם פי כל זמאן וכל מכאן, פאן אלאסיר אד'א אנטלק מן אסרתה, ואלעבד אד'א פך רקבתה, ואלמדיון אד'א אדי דינה, ואלתלמיד' אד'א גאב ען אסתאד'ה, ואלפקיר אד'א אסתגני עמא פי אידי אלנאס, לא ילזמהם אלתואצ'ע להם ואלכ'צ'וע ואלכ'שוע בין ידיהם. ואלקסם אלת'אלת' אלתואצ'ע ללה תעאלי, והו שאמל אלוג'וב עלי ג'מיע אלנאטקין, ולאזם להם פי כל זמאן ופי כל מכאן, ואליה קצדנא פי הד'א אלבאב. ואלמתואצ'ע הו אלמסמי פי כתאב אללה עניו, ונבזה בעיניו, וצנוע, ודכא, ושפל רוח, ורוח נשברה, ונדכה, ורך לבב, ונכה רוח, ולב נשבר, ונפש שחה. ומא ג'רי לנא מן אלכלאם פי אלתואצ'ע עלי אלאטלאק ליס נעני אלא הד'א אלקסם אלת'לאת', אלד'י הו אלדרג'ה אלעליא מן אלתואצ'ע. ומן צח לה לם יבעד עליה טריק אלתקרב אלי אללה ואלתזלף לדיה, וקבל אללה מנה עמלה ורצ'י ענה, כקולה זבחי אלהים רוח נשברה לב נשבר ונדכה אלהים לא תבזה. פצל. ג. ואמא אלאסבאב אלתי ענהא יחדת' אלכ'שוע ואלכ'צ'וע ואלתואצ'ע ללאנסאן בעד תשאמכ'ה פעשרה.
en_candidate:
Humility is divided into three divisions.

**The first** is general to the human and to many of the kinds of the non-rational animal. It is the dullness of the soul and its bearing-with-patience the harm it could ward off, out of its ignorance of the aspects of warding it off. This is found among the ignorant of people and the populace, on account of the slightness of their acquaintance, and the weakness of their discrimination of themselves and their measures. This is called "humility" only by way of convention; in true reality it is the weakness of the soul and its blindness from the ignorance overwhelming it concerning what would set it right — as the Friend said: "For You have hidden their heart from understanding; therefore You shall not exalt them" (Job 17:4).

True humility is what occurs after the elevation of aspiration, and the lofty disdain for sharing with the beasts in the blameworthy traits, and the towering above resemblance to the traits of the lowly populace — by surpassing knowledge, dignity of soul, and the true reality of acquaintance with the excellences and the vices. When upon this there follow the abasement of the soul and its self-lowering, this is praiseworthy. What is other than this does not enter into the praiseworthy traits and the excellences of the soul; rather it enters into their blameworthy ones. For its possessor's reckoning in this is the reckoning of the beasts.

**The second division** is humility before people. It is either on account of their dominion over him — like the captive in the hand of his enemy and the slave in the presence of his master — or on account of his poverty toward them and the emphatic need of his to what is in their hand: like the hireling toward his employer, the poor man toward the help of the wealthy man, the disciple toward his teacher. Or it may be on account of an obligatory right and a binding debt upon him that the human is unable to discharge — and so humility and abasement to the holder of the right are binding upon him, as the Wise One said: "The borrower is slave to the lender" (Proverbs 22:7). Or it may be on account of his knowledge of his falling-short in the kinds of cultivation of this world and the next, and his ignorance of the road of guidance — so that, when his hand obtains a prophet of his time, or a saint who guides, or one who calls to the path of right-direction, he humbles himself before him and lowers himself in his presence — as our early ones (peace be upon them) said: "The service of [the wise] is greater than the learning from them, as it is said: 'Here is Elisha son of Shaphat, who poured water upon the hands of Elijah' (2 Kings 3:11) — it does not say 'who learned' but 'who poured'; this teaches that the service of them is greater than the learning from them" (b. Berakhot 7b); and He said: "And his servant Joshua son of Nun, a youth, did not depart from the tent" (Exodus 33:11); and the Wise One said of the totality of the populace: "The slave of the fool is to the wise of heart" (Proverbs 11:29).
